def: The combination of two companies into a single legal entity or group.

formal.ex: The proposed [[merger]] remains subject to clearance by the competition authorities.

everyday.ex: The two French entities are going to [[merge]] next year, so we'll end up with one employer instead of two.

informal.ex: The trade press has been speculating about a [[tie-up]] for weeks.

note_fr: « Fusion » ne se dit pas « fusion » (physique, cuisine) mais « merger ». On fusionne « with » quelqu'un. « M&A » se prononce lettre à lettre : « em and ay ».

def: The purchase of a company or business by another company.

formal.ex: Following the [[acquisition]] of the entire share capital, the Company became a wholly owned subsidiary of the Group.

everyday.ex: Nobody on the shop floor saw the [[takeover]] coming.

informal.ex: A US group has just [[snapped up]] their main competitor.

note_fr: « Takeover » suggère une prise de contrôle parfois subie ; « buyout » un rachat par les dirigeants ou par un fonds. « Repurchase » et « buyback » désignent le rachat par une société de ses propres actions : faux ami pour « rachat ».

def: A transaction in which the buyer acquires the shares of the company that employs the staff, so that the employer itself does not change.

formal.ex: The transaction is structured as a [[share purchase]], and the employing entity will therefore remain unchanged.
formal.ex_us: The transaction is structured as a [[stock purchase]], and the employing entity will therefore remain unchanged.

everyday.ex: It's a [[share deal]], so nobody's contract moves - the employer stays the same.
everyday.ex_us: It's a [[stock deal]], so nobody's contract moves - the employer stays the same.

collocations: to structure the transaction as a share deal
to acquire the entire share capital
note_fr: Dans un share deal, l'employeur reste le même : pas de transfert des contrats, mais le CSE doit tout de même être consulté sur le changement de contrôle. UK « shares », US « stock ».

fr: cession d'actifs, cession de fonds de commerce
def: A transaction in which the buyer acquires a business or specific assets and not the company's shares, so that the employees change employer.

formal.ex: In the event of an [[asset purchase]], the contracts of the employees assigned to the business will pass to the Purchaser by operation of law.

everyday.ex: If we go for an [[asset deal]], the staff move across automatically - that's the law in France.

collocations: to buy the business and assets
note_fr: En France et au Royaume-Uni (TUPE), les contrats suivent l'activité cédée. Aux États-Unis, rien d'automatique : l'acquéreur choisit qui il réembauche. Prévenez d'emblée un interlocuteur américain.

def: The acquisition of a company financed largely by debt, which is then repaid out of the company's own cash flow.

formal.ex: The Company was acquired by way of a [[leveraged buyout]] led by Halden Capital.

everyday.ex: This is the company's third [[LBO]] in ten years, so the management team knows the drill.

informal.ex: Since the [[buyout]], every spare euro has gone on servicing the debt.

note_fr: UK « LEE-veridged », US « LEV-eridged ». « To be under LBO » se comprend en France, mais un natif dira « to be private-equity-backed » ou « PE-owned ».

def: An investment firm that buys companies with its investors' money, typically in order to sell them a few years later at a profit.

formal.ex: The [[financial sponsor]] intends to realise its investment within five years.
formal.ex_us: The [[financial sponsor]] intends to realize its investment within five years.

everyday.ex: Our [[private equity owner]] wants a monthly update on headcount and on anything that might reach the press.

informal.ex: She has worked for three [[PE houses]] and knows exactly what they want to see in a report.
informal.ex_us: She has worked for three [[PE shops]] and knows exactly what they want to see in a report.

note_fr: « Fund » désigne le véhicule, « firm » ou « house » la société de gestion. « Equity » = capitaux propres (jamais « équité ») et se prononce EK-wi-ti. Dans un LBO, « the sponsor » est le fonds, pas un mécène.

def: A business set up and owned jointly by two or more companies that otherwise remain separate.

formal.ex: Each party shall second employees to the [[joint venture]] for an initial term of three years.

everyday.ex: About sixty of our engineers will move into the [[JV]] in January.

collocations: to set up a joint venture
note_fr: Pas de trait d'union en anglais. La question RH à poser tout de suite : les salariés sont-ils détachés (« seconded ») ou transférés (« transferred ») à la JV ?

def: The separation of a business unit from its parent group so that it can be sold or run as a separate company.

formal.ex: The [[carve-out]] of the Coatings division will be effected by contributing the business to a newly incorporated company.

everyday.ex: They're [[carving out]] the French logistics business and selling it to a fund.

collocations: to carve a business out of the group
note_fr: Nom avec trait d'union, verbe à particule sans. Pour « périmètre », « scope » est plus naturel que « perimeter ». Enjeu RH typique : l'affectation des salariés qui travaillent pour plusieurs activités (« shared employees »).

def: The sale by a group of a business, subsidiary or asset that it no longer wishes to keep.

formal.ex: The Board has approved the [[disposal]] of the Group's non-core activities in France.
formal.ex_us: The Board has approved the [[divestiture]] of the Company's non-core operations in France.

everyday.ex: The group is [[selling off]] everything that isn't core.

informal.ex: Head office has been trying to [[offload]] the plant for two years.

collocations: to put a business up for sale
note_fr: « Cession » ne se traduit pas par « cession » (rare : cession de territoire ou de droits). Dites « sale », « disposal » (UK) ou « divestiture » (US).

def: The separation of part of a group into a new independent company, usually by distributing its shares to the existing shareholders.

formal.ex: The [[demerger]] of the Consumer division is expected to take effect in the second half of the year.
formal.ex_us: The [[spin-off]] of the Consumer division is expected to take effect in the second half of the year.

everyday.ex: They've decided to [[spin off]] the services arm and list it separately.

collocations: to split the group in two
note_fr: « Spin-off » est compris partout ; « demerger » est strictement britannique. À distinguer du « carve-out », où l'activité est le plus souvent vendue à un tiers.

def: The process of restoring a loss-making or failing business to profitability.

formal.ex: The Board has asked the Chief Executive to present a [[turnaround plan]] by the end of the quarter.

everyday.ex: We've got eighteen months to [[turn the business around]].

informal.ex: It took two years and a new management team to [[get back on track]].

note_fr: « Recovery » seul désigne plutôt la reprise économique. Le redressement judiciaire français se glose « court-supervised reorganisation proceedings » ; « administration » (UK) et « Chapter 11 » (US) n'en sont que des équivalents approximatifs.

def: A deliberate reduction in the number of people a company employs.

formal.ex: The Company does not envisage any [[workforce reduction]] as a result of the transaction.
formal.ex_us: The Company does not anticipate any [[reduction in force]] as a result of the transaction.

everyday.ex: After two rounds of [[downsizing]], the people who are left are stretched very thin.

informal.ex: They want to [[slim down]] the support functions before the sale.

note_fr: « Right-sizing » est l'euphémisme managérial ; « RIF » (prononcé « riff ») est américain. Au Royaume-Uni, le terme juridique est « redundancies ». « Reduction of effectives » n'existe pas.

def: A company that is owned or controlled by another company.

formal.ex: Brevane SAS is a [[wholly owned subsidiary]] of Brevane Holdings Ltd.

everyday.ex: The French [[subsidiary]] has its own works council and its own collective agreements.

collocations: the French subsidiary of a US group
note_fr: « Filiale » ≠ « filial » (relatif aux enfants) ni « affiliate » (société liée, lien plus lâche). « Branch » = succursale sans personnalité morale : la différence compte pour savoir qui est l'employeur.

def: The two key stages of a transaction: signing, when the parties commit themselves, and completion, when ownership actually passes.

formal.ex: [[Completion]] shall take place ten business days after the last of the conditions has been satisfied.
formal.ex_us: The [[closing]] shall take place ten business days after the last of the conditions has been satisfied.

everyday.ex: We sign in March and hope to [[complete]] by the end of June.
everyday.ex_us: We sign in March and hope to [[close]] by the end of June.

note_fr: UK « completion », US « closing » (de plus en plus entendu à Londres). En France, le CSE doit être consulté avant que la décision soit prise, donc en pratique avant le signing de l'accord engageant : c'est ce qui surprend les équipes anglo-saxonnes.

def: A short preliminary document recording the main terms the parties have agreed in principle, usually not legally binding as to the deal itself.

formal.ex: The [[heads of terms]] are expressed to be non-binding, save for the exclusivity and confidentiality provisions.
formal.ex_us: The [[letter of intent]] is expressly non-binding, except for the exclusivity and confidentiality provisions.

everyday.ex: We've agreed [[heads of terms]], but nothing is binding yet.
everyday.ex_us: We've signed an [[LOI]], but nothing is binding yet.

note_fr: « Heads of terms » est toujours pluriel. Un document non engageant peut en général être signé avant la consultation du CSE ; un accord ferme, non : la nuance « binding / non-binding » est donc capitale.

fr: promesse d'achat consentie par l'acquéreur (put option)
def: In French deal practice, a unilateral undertaking by the buyer to acquire the business on agreed terms, which the seller may accept once its works council has been consulted.

formal.ex: Under the [[put option agreement]], the Purchaser irrevocably undertakes to acquire the Business if the Seller exercises the option once the works council consultation has been completed.

everyday.ex: We'll use a [[put option]]: the buyer commits now, and we only sign the sale agreement once the works council has given its opinion.

note_fr: Mécanisme propre à la pratique française, à expliquer systématiquement : l'acquéreur s'engage seul, le vendeur reste libre tant que le CSE n'a pas rendu son avis. Les Anglo-Saxons connaissent le « put » financier, pas cet usage.

explain.written: Because a French seller must consult its works council before committing to a sale, the buyer first grants a put option - a unilateral promise to buy on the agreed terms - and the sale agreement itself is signed only once the consultation has been completed.
explain.spoken: In France the seller can't sign before its works council has been consulted, so the buyer commits first through a put option and the seller signs afterwards.

def: Conditions that must be satisfied before the parties are obliged to complete the transaction.

formal.ex: Completion is subject to the satisfaction of the [[conditions precedent]] set out in Schedule 2.
formal.ex_us: The closing is subject to satisfaction of the [[conditions to closing]] set forth in Article 7.

everyday.ex: The only [[CPs]] left are merger clearance and the labour inspector's sign-off on the two representatives.
everyday.ex_us: The only [[closing conditions]] left are antitrust clearance and the labor inspector's sign-off on the two representatives.

note_fr: « Suspensive condition » est un calque. Dans cette expression, l'adjectif est postposé et se prononce « pri-SEE-dent ». En France, on évite de faire de la consultation du CSE une simple condition suspensive d'un accord déjà ferme : elle doit le précéder.

def: The final date by which the conditions must be satisfied, failing which either party may walk away from the deal.

formal.ex: If the conditions have not been satisfied by the [[long-stop date]], either party may terminate this Agreement.
formal.ex_us: If the conditions have not been satisfied by the [[outside date]], either party may terminate this Agreement.

everyday.ex: The [[long-stop date]] leaves us very little margin if the consultation overruns.
everyday.ex_us: The [[drop-dead date]] leaves us very little room if the consultation runs over.

collocations: to walk away from the deal
note_fr: « Long-stop » vient du cricket ; les Américains disent « outside date » ou, familièrement, « drop-dead date ». « Limit date » est un calque : hors contrat, « final deadline » suffit.

def: The investigation a buyer carries out into a target business before committing to buy it.

formal.ex: The Purchaser has carried out a [[due diligence exercise]] covering all employment matters.
formal.ex_us: The Purchaser has conducted a [[due diligence review]] covering all employment matters.

everyday.ex: We're doing the HR [[due diligence]] this week, and the picture is better than I expected.

informal.ex: The [[DD]] turned up two unpleasant surprises on overtime.

note_fr: Indénombrable : « a due diligence » est un calque fréquent ; dites « a due diligence exercise / review ». « Audit » évoque d'abord, en anglais, l'audit des comptes.

def: A secure, usually online, space in which the seller makes confidential documents available to prospective buyers.

formal.ex: All collective agreements in force have been uploaded to the [[virtual data room]].

everyday.ex: I can't find the payroll files in the [[data room]] - can you chase the seller?

informal.ex: Everything you need should be in the [[VDR]] by tonight.

collocations: to upload documents to the data room
to raise a question through the Q&A process
note_fr: On y place des données salariales anonymisées ou agrégées (« an anonymised employee census »), pas les dossiers individuels. « Data » : DAY-ta au Royaume-Uni ; DAY-ta ou DA-ta aux États-Unis.

def: A warning sign of a serious problem or risk identified during a review.

formal.ex: The review identified two [[material issues]] relating to working time.

everyday.ex: The biggest [[red flag]] is the way they've been using fixed-term contracts.

informal.ex: It's a concern, but I wouldn't call it a [[deal-breaker]].

note_fr: « To flag » = signaler (« I just wanted to flag that... »), verbe très courant. « Alert point » est un calque. En droit, « material » signifie significatif, non « matériel ».

def: Debts or legal obligations that a company owes or may come to owe, such as unpaid wages, accrued holiday or potential claims.

formal.ex: The Seller shall remain responsible for all [[employment liabilities]] arising before the Transfer Date.

everyday.ex: Our [[exposure]] on unpaid overtime could run into seven figures.

note_fr: « Liability » = dette ou responsabilité juridique, à ne pas confondre avec « reliability » (fiabilité). Provisionner : « to make a provision » (UK), « to set up a reserve » ou « to accrue » (US). « Passif social » n'a pas d'équivalent figé.

def: The number of people employed by a company or working in a team.

formal.ex: The [[number of employees]] assigned to the Business as at the reference date is set out in Schedule 4.
formal.ex_us: The [[number of employees]] assigned to the Business as of the reference date is set forth in Schedule 4.

everyday.ex: Total [[headcount]] is 412, which works out at about 390 full-time equivalents.

informal.ex: We're about twenty [[heads]] over budget in the support functions.

note_fr: « Effectives » n'existe pas dans ce sens. Distinguez « headcount » (personnes physiques) et « FTEs » (équivalents temps plein). « Staff » est un collectif : « the staff are » (UK), « the staff is » (US).

def: The total cost to the employer of paying its workforce, including salaries, bonuses and employer social security contributions.

formal.ex: [[Total staff costs]], including employer social security contributions, represent a little over a third of revenue.
formal.ex_us: [[Total compensation expense]], including employer payroll taxes, represents a little over a third of revenue.

everyday.ex: [[The wage bill]] has gone up sharply since the last pay round.
everyday.ex_us: [[Payroll]] has gone up sharply since the last pay cycle.

collocations: to keep staff costs under control
note_fr: « Salary mass » est un calque à bannir. Précisez toujours si le chiffre est chargé (« fully loaded », « including employer contributions ») : le niveau des charges patronales françaises surprend les lecteurs anglo-saxons.

def: Legal claims that have been brought against the company and have not yet been decided or settled.

formal.ex: Details of all [[pending and threatened litigation]] involving current or former employees are set out in the Disclosure Letter.
formal.ex_us: Details of all [[pending and threatened litigation]] involving current or former employees are set forth in the Disclosure Schedules.

everyday.ex: There are eleven [[ongoing tribunal claims]], most of them about overtime.
everyday.ex_us: There are eleven [[open lawsuits]], most of them over overtime.

note_fr: « Contentious » = qui prête à controverse ; « contentieux » se dit « litigation » ou « claims ». Le conseil de prud'hommes se glose « the employment tribunal » (UK) ou « the French labor court » (US).

def: Statements of fact about the business that the seller gives the buyer in the sale agreement, and for which it is liable if they prove untrue.

formal.ex: The employment [[warranties]] are qualified by the matters fairly disclosed in the data room.
formal.ex_us: The employment [[representations and warranties]] are qualified by the matters set forth in the disclosure schedules.

everyday.ex: We need the seller to give [[warranties]] on compliance with the working-time rules.
everyday.ex_us: We need the seller to give [[reps and warranties]] on wage-and-hour compliance.

note_fr: « Warranty » ≠ « guarantee » (engagement d'un tiers garant ou garantie commerciale). Les praticiens anglais parlent de « warranties », les Américains de « reps and warranties ».

def: An undertaking by the seller to reimburse the buyer in full for a particular, identified liability if it materialises.

formal.ex: The Seller shall grant the Purchaser a [[specific indemnity]] in respect of the pending social security audit.
formal.ex_us: The Seller shall grant the Purchaser a [[specific indemnity]] with respect to the pending social security audit.

everyday.ex: We need [[to be covered]] for anything that comes out of the social security audit.

collocations: to indemnify the buyer against a loss
note_fr: « Indemnity » ici ≠ indemnité versée au salarié (« severance », « compensation »). La « garantie de passif » se rend, selon le cas, par « warranties » (générales) ou « specific indemnity » (risque identifié).

def: Acting as if the deal had already completed - for instance by integrating teams or sharing sensitive information - before clearance has been obtained or ownership has passed.

formal.ex: Any [[premature implementation of the transaction]] may expose both parties to substantial fines.

everyday.ex: We can plan the integration, but giving instructions to their managers before we own the business would be [[gun-jumping]].

informal.ex: Let's not [[jump the gun]] - they're still a competitor until the deal goes through.

note_fr: Avant la réalisation, on planifie mais on n'intègre pas : pas d'instructions aux équipes de la cible, pas d'échange de données salariales individuelles hors « clean team ». « To jump the gun » : agir trop tôt (image du faux départ).

term.uk: to inform and consult the works council
term.us: to inform and consult the works council

ipa.uk: /tu ɪnˌfɔːm ən kənˌsʌlt ðə ˈwɜːks ˌkaʊns(ə)l/
ipa.us: /tu ɪnˌfɔːrm ən kənˌsʌlt ðə ˈwɜːrks ˌkaʊns(ə)l/

def: To give the elected employee representatives full information about a proposed decision and obtain their opinion before the decision is taken.

formal.ex: The [[information and consultation process]] must be completed before any binding agreement is entered into.

everyday.ex: In France we have [[to consult the works council]] before we sign, not after.

note_fr: Tant que l'avis n'est pas rendu, parlez de « proposed » ou « contemplated transaction » : un e-mail affirmant « the decision has been made » peut suffire à nourrir une action pour délit d'entrave. « Consult » est transitif : « consult the works council ».

explain.written: Under French law, the employer must inform and consult its works council (comité social et économique, or CSE) on any proposed change in the ownership or organisation of the company before the decision is finally taken; the council gives an opinion but has no veto.
explain.spoken: Before we commit to anything, we have to present the project to the elected staff representatives and get their opinion. They can't block the deal, but we can't skip the step.

def: The formal view, favourable or not, that the works council expresses at the end of a consultation; it does not bind the employer.

formal.ex: The works council [[delivered its opinion]] on the proposed sale at its last meeting.

everyday.ex: Once the works council has [[given its opinion]], we're free to sign - whatever the opinion says.

collocations: to be deemed to have been consulted
note_fr: « Advice » = conseil ; l'avis du CSE est « an opinion ». Insistez sur les deux faces : avis purement consultatif (« no veto »), mais étape incontournable. Faute d'avis dans le délai, le CSE est réputé avoir rendu un avis négatif.

explain.written: The works council's opinion (avis) closes the consultation: it is advisory only, and if the council does not respond within the applicable time limit it is deemed to have given a negative opinion.
explain.spoken: They give their view at the end. It's purely advisory - even a no doesn't stop us - but we do have to wait for it.

def: The schedule of meetings and deadlines within which the employee representatives must be consulted.

formal.ex: The [[consultation period]] starts to run when the works council receives the written information on the proposed transaction.

everyday.ex: Realistically, the [[consultation timetable]] adds one to three months before we can sign.
everyday.ex_us: Realistically, the [[consultation timeline]] adds one to three months before we can sign.

collocations: to build the consultation into the deal timetable
to agree a timetable with the works council
note_fr: « Delay » = retard, pas délai : dites « time limit », « period » ou « deadline ». « Planning » n'est pas un nom de calendrier en anglais. UK « timetable », US « timeline » ou « schedule ».

fr: transfert automatique des contrats de travail
def: The rule under which, when a business changes hands, the employees assigned to it move to the new owner with their contracts unchanged, without anyone having to agree.

formal.uk: to transfer by operation of law
formal.us: to transfer by operation of law
formal.ex: The employment contracts of the employees assigned to the Business shall [[transfer by operation of law]] to the Purchaser on the Transfer Date.

everyday.ex: Their contracts [[transfer automatically]] - nobody signs anything, and nobody can opt out.

informal.ex: Everyone in the warehouse [[moves across]] on the same terms.

collocations: on their existing terms and conditions
to move to the new owner
note_fr: Équivalent britannique : TUPE (prononcé « tioupi »). Aux États-Unis, pas de transfert automatique : l'acquéreur d'actifs fait des offres d'embauche. « By operation of law » = de plein droit.

def: The employees whose contracts pass to the buyer as part of a business transfer.

formal.ex: The Seller shall provide the Purchaser with an up-to-date list of [[the Transferring Employees]] no later than ten business days before Completion.

everyday.ex: We need to agree exactly who [[the people in scope]] are before we talk to the works council.

collocations: to be wholly or mainly assigned to
note_fr: « In scope / out of scope » est le jargon courant. « Transferring » avant le transfert, « transferred » après. Point sensible : les salariés qui ne travaillent qu'en partie pour l'activité cédée.

fr: cédant et cessionnaire (ancien et nouvel employeur)
def: The employer that hands over the business (the transferor) and the employer that takes it on (the transferee).

formal.ex: The respective obligations of [[the transferor and the transferee]] towards the employees are set out in clause 11.
formal.ex_us: The respective obligations of [[the transferor and the transferee]] toward the employees are set forth in Section 11.

everyday.ex: [[The outgoing and incoming employers]] ought to write to the staff together.

note_fr: Accent tonique : transFERor mais transferEE (comme employEE). En France, le nouvel employeur reprend en principe les obligations de l'ancien envers les salariés à la date du transfert, sauf exceptions ; la répartition finale entre les deux se règle dans le contrat de cession.

def: An organised grouping of people and assets that pursues an activity with its own objective; if it keeps its identity after changing hands, the employees' contracts transfer with it.

formal.uk: an economic entity which retains its identity
formal.us: an economic entity which retains its identity
formal.ex: The automatic transfer applies only where the activity constitutes [[an economic entity which retains its identity]] in the hands of the new operator.

everyday.ex: The question is whether the maintenance team is really [[a self-standing business]] or just a few people from a bigger department.

note_fr: Notion issue du droit européen : la formule consacrée est « an economic entity which retains its identity ». Si le critère n'est pas rempli, pas de transfert automatique : il faut l'accord individuel de chaque salarié.

def: A transfer of only part of a company's business, which raises the question of which employees and which representatives go with it.

formal.uk: transfer of part of the business
formal.us: transfer of part of the business
formal.ex: On a [[transfer of part of the business]], the transfer of an employee representative's contract requires the prior authorisation of the labour inspector.
formal.ex_us: On a [[transfer of part of the business]], the transfer of an employee representative's contract requires the prior authorization of the labor inspector.

everyday.ex: Because it's only a [[partial transfer]], the two reps in scope can't move until the labour inspector says yes.
everyday.ex_us: Because it's only a [[partial transfer]], the two reps in scope can't move until the labor inspector says yes.

collocations: to be assigned mainly to the transferred activity
note_fr: Piège de calendrier : en cas de transfert partiel, le transfert des représentants du personnel suppose l'autorisation préalable de l'inspecteur du travail. À anticiper bien avant la réalisation ; rien de tel au Royaume-Uni ni aux États-Unis.

def: The principle that an employee's period of service is treated as unbroken when the employer changes.

formal.ex: The Transferring Employees' [[continuity of employment]] shall be preserved, and their service with the Seller shall count as service with the Purchaser.

everyday.ex: You [[carry over your service]] in full, so nothing that depends on it changes.

note_fr: « Seniority » au sens d'ancienneté est surtout américain ; au Royaume-Uni, on dit « length of service ». « Seniority recovery » est un calque : dites « past service is recognised ».

def: To refuse, as an employee, to move to the new employer in a business transfer.

formal.ex: Where the statutory conditions are met, an employee is not entitled [[to object to the transfer]] of his or her contract.

everyday.ex: What if somebody [[refuses to transfer]]? In France they can't, really - the contract moves whether they like it or not.

informal.ex: There's no way [[to opt out]] of the transfer here, unlike in the UK.

collocations: to have no right to object
note_fr: Différence majeure : au Royaume-Uni (TUPE), le salarié peut « object », et son contrat prend alors fin sans licenciement ; en France, le transfert légal s'impose aux deux parties. Construction : « to object TO + nom ou -ing ».

fr: mise en cause des accords collectifs
def: In French law, the effect of a transfer on the former employer's company-level agreements: they stop applying to the transferred employees after a limited period unless they are replaced.

formal.uk: to be automatically called into question
formal.us: to be automatically called into question
formal.ex: The collective agreements in force at the Seller will [[be automatically called into question]] as a result of the transfer.

everyday.ex: The seller's agreements don't [[fall away]] on day one - they carry on for a while so that we can negotiate.

collocations: to continue to apply for a limited period
note_fr: Ne traduisez pas par « denunciation » (dénonciation publique). Rien de comparable au Royaume-Uni, où les clauses issues d'accords collectifs sont en principe incorporées au contrat et suivent le salarié.

explain.written: On a transfer, the transferor's collective agreements are automatically 'called into question' (mise en cause): they continue to apply to the transferred employees for a limited period, during which the new employer must negotiate a replacement.
explain.spoken: The old employer's agreements don't follow people for ever. They keep applying for a while - a bit over a year at most - and in that time we have to negotiate something to replace them.

def: The limited period during which the former employer's collective agreements go on applying to transferred employees after a transfer.

formal.ex: During the [[survival period]], the Transferring Employees shall continue to benefit from the Seller's company agreements.

everyday.ex: Their working-time agreement [[carries on applying]] for up to fifteen months unless we agree something new sooner.

collocations: a notice period followed by twelve months
until a substitution agreement is signed
note_fr: Calque assumé : « survival period » ne dit rien à un Anglo-Saxon sans explication ; glosez par « transitional period ». Durée : un préavis, puis douze mois au plus, sauf accord de substitution conclu entre-temps.

explain.written: The 'survival period' is the time during which the transferor's collective agreements continue to apply after the transfer - a notice period followed by up to twelve months - unless a substitution agreement is concluded earlier.
explain.spoken: It's a grace period: the old agreements keep running for up to about fifteen months while we negotiate the new one.

def: A collective agreement negotiated after a transfer or merger to replace the agreements that previously applied to the transferred employees.

formal.ex: The Purchaser intends to open negotiations with a view to concluding a [[substitution agreement]] within six months of the Transfer Date.

everyday.ex: If we sign a [[replacement agreement]] by the summer, everyone will be on the same terms from January.

collocations: to preserve the level of pay
note_fr: À défaut d'accord dans le délai, les salariés transférés ne conservent qu'une garantie de rémunération. La loi permet aussi d'anticiper cette négociation avant le transfert : utile à dire à un acquéreur pressé.

explain.written: A substitution agreement (accord de substitution) is the company-level agreement negotiated with the unions after a transfer to replace the transferor's agreements; once signed, it applies in their place.
explain.spoken: It's the new agreement we negotiate with the unions to replace the ones people brought with them.

def: Bringing the pay, benefits and working arrangements of employees from different companies into line after a merger or transfer.

formal.ex: The [[harmonisation of terms and conditions]] will be the subject of negotiations with the representative trade unions.
formal.ex_us: The [[harmonization of terms and conditions]] will be the subject of negotiations with the representative labor unions.

everyday.uk: to bring everyone onto the same terms
everyday.us: to bring everyone onto the same terms
everyday.ex: It'll take us a good year [[to bring everyone onto the same terms]].

note_fr: « Statut » ≠ « status » : dites « terms and conditions » ou « package ». Au Royaume-Uni, modifier les conditions en raison même du transfert est très encadré par TUPE : vos collègues britanniques s'étonneront qu'en France l'harmonisation passe par la négociation collective.

def: To align different groups of employees on the more generous of their respective terms.

formal.uk: to align on the more favourable terms
formal.us: to align on the more favorable terms
formal.ex: The unions are asking for all benefits to be [[aligned on the more favourable terms]].
formal.ex_us: The unions are asking for all benefits to be [[aligned on the more favorable terms]].

everyday.ex: We can't afford [[to level up]] across the board, so we'll have to trade some things off.

informal.ex: The unions will try [[to cherry-pick]] the best of both packages.

collocations: to trade one benefit off against another
note_fr: « Level up / level down » : aligner par le haut / par le bas. « Cherry-picking » (prendre le meilleur de chaque statut) est le mot que les financiers comprennent immédiatement.

fr: maintien du salaire à titre personnel
def: Allowing existing employees to keep, on a personal basis, a rate of pay or a benefit that is higher than the new scheme provides.

formal.uk: pay protection on a personal basis
formal.ex: Employees whose current salary exceeds the new scale will receive [[pay protection on a personal basis]].
formal.ex_us: Employees whose current salary exceeds the new range will keep it under [[grandfathered terms]].

everyday.ex: Anyone above the new band will [[be red-circled]] until the scale catches up.
everyday.ex_us: Anyone above the new range will [[be grandfathered]] until the range catches up.

note_fr: « Red-circling » vise surtout la rémunération ; « grandfathering » (américain, compris partout) tout droit maintenu au profit des anciens. « Legacy terms » = conditions héritées de l'ancien employeur.

def: The process of combining two organisations - their people, systems and ways of working - once a deal has completed.

formal.ex: Responsibility for [[post-merger integration]] rests with a steering committee chaired by the Chief Operating Officer.

everyday.ex: The deal was the easy part; the [[integration]] is where it usually goes wrong.

informal.ex: She ran the [[PMI]] on their last two acquisitions.

note_fr: « PMI » est un sigle de consultants ; en France il évoque les petites et moyennes industries, donc explicitez-le. Si l'opération n'est pas une fusion au sens strict, dites « post-acquisition integration ».

fr: premier jour après la réalisation (Day One)
def: The first day on which the business operates under its new owner or as a separate company.

formal.ex: The HR workstream has confirmed [[Day One readiness]] for payroll, benefits and employee communications.

everyday.ex: On [[day one]], people need to be paid, to know who their manager is and to have a badge that works - everything else can wait.

collocations: to be ready for Day One
note_fr: Sans article : « on day one ». Par extension, « from day one » = dès le début. Pour un système informatique, on parle plutôt de « go-live ».

def: An agreement under which the seller goes on providing services such as payroll or IT to the business it has sold for a limited time after completion.

formal.ex: Payroll will continue to be processed by the Seller under the [[transitional services agreement]] for a period of nine months.
formal.ex_us: Payroll will continue to be processed by the Seller under the [[transition services agreement]] for a period of nine months.

everyday.ex: Payroll stays with the seller under the [[TSA]] until we've got our own system up and running.

note_fr: Se prononce lettre à lettre. Vigilance RH : les salariés du vendeur qui rendent le service ne sont pas transférés, et la fin du TSA (paie, SIRH, mutuelle) est un jalon à risque.

def: As an independent business, without relying on the support functions, systems or schemes of the former parent group.

formal.ex: The cost of running the HR function [[on a standalone basis]] has been estimated in the separation plan.

everyday.uk: to stand on its own two feet
everyday.us: to stand on its own two feet
everyday.ex: The business has never had its own payroll or HR system, so it'll take time [[to stand on its own two feet]].

note_fr: Dans un carve-out, recensez tout ce qui dépend du groupe : mutuelle, prévoyance, épargne salariale, SIRH. « To stand up a function » (la créer de toutes pièces) est du jargon projet, surtout américain.

def: The savings or extra revenue expected from combining two businesses.

formal.ex: The business plan assumes substantial [[cost synergies]], roughly half of which relate to support functions.

everyday.ex: When they say synergies, what they mean is [[savings]] - and in the support functions that means jobs.

informal.ex: There's a lot of [[overlap]] between the two finance teams.

note_fr: Prononcez SIN-er-djiz (« g » doux). Pour des représentants du personnel, « synergies » veut presque toujours dire suppressions de postes : pesez le mot. « Doublons » = « duplicate roles » ou « overlap ».

def: Conflict or misunderstanding that arises when organisations with different values and working habits are brought together.

formal.ex: [[Cultural integration]] has been identified as one of the principal risks to the success of the merger.

everyday.ex: It's a classic [[culture clash]]: a family-owned French company and a US group that runs everything by the quarterly numbers.

informal.ex: Six months on, there's still a lot of [[us and them]] between the two sites.

note_fr: « Culture shock » concerne une personne à l'étranger ; pour deux organisations, on dit « culture clash ». « Corporate culture » = culture d'entreprise.

def: The formal relationships that show who is accountable to whom in an organisation.

formal.ex: The new [[reporting lines]] will take effect on Completion and will be communicated to all managers beforehand.
formal.ex_us: The new [[reporting lines]] will take effect at Closing and will be communicated to all managers beforehand.

everyday.ex: People don't care about the legal structure; they want to know [[who reports to whom]].

note_fr: « Hierarchical line » et « my hierarchy » sont des calques : dites « my line manager », « senior management ». Rattachement fonctionnel = « dotted line » ; hiérarchique = « solid line ». « N+1 » n'existe pas en anglais.

def: A payment promised to an employee on condition that he or she is still with the company on a given date.

formal.ex: The [[retention bonus]] shall be payable provided that the Employee is still employed, and not under notice, on the payment date.

everyday.ex: We've offered the plant manager a [[retention bonus]] payable six months after the deal closes.
everyday.ex_us: We've offered the plant manager a [[stay bonus]] payable six months after the deal closes.

informal.ex: The scheme is basically [[golden handcuffs]] for the top twelve.

collocations: to be conditional on continued employment
note_fr: En anglais, « retention » est neutre (fidélisation), sans la connotation négative de « rétention ». Condition de présence : « conditional on continued employment ». « Golden handcuffs » est familier mais courant, y compris dans la presse.

def: The risk that the business will suffer if a small number of people with critical skills or relationships leave.

formal.ex: The report highlights a significant [[key-person dependency]] in the research and development team.

everyday.ex: If we lose three or four [[key people]] in the first six months, the business case falls apart.

informal.ex: The sales director is a serious [[flight risk]] - she's already had two calls from headhunters.

collocations: to be approached by a competitor
note_fr: « Key man » a vieilli : préférez « key person ». « A flight risk » qualifie la personne susceptible de partir (« she's a flight risk »).

def: The rate at which employees leave a company and have to be replaced.

formal.ex: The voluntary [[attrition rate]] almost doubled in the twelve months following the announcement.

everyday.ex: [[Staff turnover]] has nearly doubled since the announcement.
everyday.ex_us: [[Turnover]] has nearly doubled since the announcement.

informal.ex: Several engineers [[jumped ship]] as soon as the sale was announced.

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, « turnover » seul signifie chiffre d'affaires : précisez « staff turnover ». « Attrition » désigne aussi les départs naturels non remplacés (« natural wastage », UK).

def: A change in who ultimately owns or controls a company, which may trigger rights under certain contracts.

formal.ex: The Chief Executive's contract contains a [[change-of-control clause]] entitling him to an enhanced severance payment.

everyday.ex: Does a [[change of control]] trigger anything in the top team's contracts?

informal.ex: Two of the directors have a [[golden parachute]] if the company is sold.

collocations: to be triggered by the sale
note_fr: Point classique de due diligence : les clauses « triggered by » la cession. « To control » = diriger, maîtriser ; « contrôler » au sens de vérifier se dit « to check ».

def: The arrangement by which the managers of a company under LBO invest alongside the fund and share in the gain when it sells.

formal.ex: Participation in the [[management incentive plan]] is offered to members of the executive committee and to a limited number of key managers.

everyday.ex: The new CFO wants to know what the [[MIP]] looks like before she signs.

informal.ex: The fund wants the top team to have real [[skin in the game]].

note_fr: « Management package » est un franglais : en anglais, « management incentive plan (MIP) » ou « management equity ». Le traitement fiscal et social français de ces gains est un sujet de spécialistes : restez générale et renvoyez aux conseils.

fr: clauses de départ (good leaver / bad leaver)
def: The terms of a management equity plan that determine what happens to a manager's shares, and at what price, depending on why he or she leaves.

formal.uk: good leaver and bad leaver provisions
formal.us: good leaver and bad leaver provisions
formal.ex: Under the [[good leaver and bad leaver provisions]], the price at which a departing manager must sell his or her shares depends on the circumstances of the departure.

everyday.ex: If she's dismissed without any misconduct, does she count as a [[good leaver]]?

collocations: to be treated as a bad leaver
note_fr: Lien direct avec le droit du travail : la qualification de « bad leaver » dépend souvent du motif de la rupture (démission, faute), d'où des contentieux. « Leaver » = personne qui part ; « quitter » est péjoratif.

def: A group of legally separate companies treated as a single employer for employee representation purposes because they share management, activities and a workforce community.

formal.ex: The three companies have been recognised as forming an [[economic and social unit]], with a single works council.
formal.ex_us: The three companies have been recognized as forming an [[economic and social unit]], with a single works council.

everyday.uk: to be treated as one company for staff representation
everyday.us: to be treated as one company for staff representation
everyday.ex: Legally they're three companies, but they're [[treated as one company for staff representation]].

collocations: to recognise a UES by agreement or by court decision
note_fr: Enjeu de l'opération : la société cédée sort de l'UES, ce qui remet en cause le périmètre des instances et, parfois, les accords conclus à ce niveau. Aux États-Unis, la notion de « single employer » en est un parent éloigné.

explain.written: An economic and social unit (unité économique et sociale, or UES) is a group of legally distinct companies recognised, by collective agreement or by a court, as a single entity for the purpose of electing employee representatives.
explain.spoken: It's a French mechanism: several companies that work as one are treated as a single company when it comes to electing staff representatives.

def: A site or unit of a company recognised as having enough management autonomy to have its own works council.

formal.ex: Following the merger, the number and boundaries of the [[distinct establishments]] will be renegotiated with the unions.

everyday.uk: a site with its own works council
everyday.us: a site with its own works council
everyday.ex: Lyon is [[a site with its own works council]], so we have a local consultation as well as the central one.

note_fr: « Establishment » évoque spontanément, en anglais, les élites ou un commerce : ajoutez « site » ou glosez. Le critère est l'autonomie de gestion du responsable de l'établissement.

explain.written: A distinct establishment (établissement distinct) is a part of the company recognised, by agreement or failing that by the employer's decision, as sufficiently autonomous in its management to have its own works council alongside the central one.
explain.spoken: Some of our sites count as separate establishments, which means each one has its own local works council under a central one.

def: The level - site, company or group of companies - at which employee representative bodies are set up and elected.

formal.uk: the scope of the employee representative bodies
formal.us: the scope of the employee representative bodies
formal.ex: The merger will require [[the scope of the employee representative bodies]] to be redefined.

everyday.ex: After the merger we'll need to sort out [[who represents whom]], and at what level.

note_fr: « Perimeter » passe en jargon de projet, mais « scope » est plus naturel. La « bargaining unit » américaine est une notion voisine, mais elle concerne la négociation syndicale et non une instance élue.

fr: maintien des mandats après un transfert
def: The rule that employee representatives keep their elected office after a transfer if the entity transferred retains its autonomy.

formal.ex: Where the transferred entity retains its autonomy, the members of its works council shall [[remain in office]] until the end of their term.

everyday.ex: If the site moves across as a whole, the reps [[keep their seats]]; if it's absorbed into our organisation, they don't.
everyday.ex_us: If the site moves across as a whole, the reps [[keep their seats]]; if it's absorbed into our organization, they don't.

note_fr: « Mandate » = mission confiée ou légitimité issue d'un vote (« a mandate to negotiate ») ; pour la durée du mandat d'un élu, dites « term of office ». Si l'entité perd son autonomie, les mandats cessent, mais la protection contre le licenciement subsiste un temps.

def: In some French sectors, such as cleaning or security, the obligation under the industry collective agreement for an incoming contractor to take on the staff assigned to a contract it has won.

formal.uk: transfer pursuant to the sector collective agreement
formal.us: transfer pursuant to the sector collective agreement
formal.ex: On a change of contractor, eligible employees are offered a [[transfer pursuant to the sector collective agreement]], which requires their express consent.

everyday.uk: to take on the incumbent's staff
everyday.us: to take on the incumbent's staff
everyday.ex: If we switch cleaning contractors, the new one has [[to take on the incumbent's staff]] under the sector agreement.

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, le changement de prestataire relève directement de TUPE (« service provision change »). En France, la simple perte d'un marché n'emporte pas le transfert légal : la reprise résulte, le cas échéant, de la convention de branche et suppose l'accord du salarié.

explain.written: Where a service contract changes hands and the statutory automatic transfer does not apply, certain French industry-wide agreements require the incoming contractor to offer employment to the staff assigned to the contract; unlike the statutory transfer, this requires each employee's consent.
explain.spoken: When a service contract changes hands in sectors like cleaning or security, the new contractor has to offer jobs to the people working on it - but each person has to agree.

def: A unit that provides support services such as payroll, accounting or HR administration to several entities of a group.

formal.ex: Payroll and HR administration for all French entities will be migrated to the Group's [[shared service centre]] in Kraków.
formal.ex_us: Payroll and HR administration for all French entities will be migrated to the Group's [[shared services center]] in Kraków.

everyday.ex: Once payroll moves to the [[SSC]], we'll only keep two people on site.

collocations: to migrate an activity to the SSC
note_fr: Évitez le sigle français « CSP » en réunion anglophone (il désigne aussi le contrat de sécurisation professionnelle). UK « centre », US « center ».

def: Having an activity carried out by an outside provider instead of the company's own employees.

formal.ex: The proposed [[outsourcing]] of facilities management will be submitted to the works council for consultation.

everyday.ex: They want [[to outsource]] payroll and bring recruitment back in-house.

informal.ex: IT support was [[farmed out]] years ago.

collocations: to outsource an activity to a provider
to bring an activity back in-house
note_fr: « Externalization » n'est pas le mot. Ne confondez pas « outsourcing » (vers un tiers) et « offshoring » (vers l'étranger) : l'un n'implique pas l'autre. En France, externaliser une entité économique autonome emporte le transfert des contrats.

def: Moving an activity to another country, usually in order to reduce costs.

formal.ex: The Company has no plans for any [[relocation of activities abroad]].

everyday.ex: The unions see the shared service centre as [[offshoring]] by another name.
everyday.ex_us: The unions see the shared services center as [[offshoring]] by another name.

informal.ex: The local paper accused the group of [[shipping jobs overseas]].

note_fr: « Delocalisation » n'est pas idiomatique. « Relocation » seul est neutre (tout déménagement). « Nearshoring » = vers un pays proche ; « reshoring » = relocalisation.

def: Moving a company's premises, and the people who work there, to a different place.

formal.ex: The [[relocation of the site]] to Villeneuve will take effect in September and remains within the same geographical area.

everyday.ex: [[The move]] adds forty minutes to some people's commute, and that's what they'll want to talk about.

note_fr: En droit français, tout dépend du « secteur géographique » : à l'intérieur, simple changement des conditions de travail ; au-delà, modification du contrat qui suppose l'accord du salarié, sauf clause de mobilité. « Premises » est toujours pluriel.

def: The financial and practical support offered to employees who move home because their job moves.

formal.ex: Employees who agree to move will be eligible for [[relocation assistance]], including removal costs and a settling-in allowance.
formal.ex_us: Employees who agree to move will be eligible for [[relocation assistance]], including moving expenses and a settling-in allowance.

everyday.ex: The [[relocation package]] is generous, but it won't persuade people with children at school.

note_fr: UK « removal costs », US « moving expenses » (aux États-Unis, « removal » évoque l'expulsion). « Accompaniment measures » est un calque : dites « support measures » ou « assistance ».

def: The structured approach used to prepare and support people through an organisational change.

formal.ex: A dedicated [[change management]] team will support line managers throughout the transition.

everyday.ex: The plan is sound on paper; the hard part is [[taking people with you]].
everyday.ex_us: The plan is sound on paper; the hard part is [[bringing people along]].

collocations: to support people through the change
note_fr: « Change conduct » n'existe pas. « To embed » = ancrer durablement. Pour « accompagner », évitez « accompany » : « to support people through the change ».

def: The reluctance or opposition people show when their working environment or habits are changed.

formal.ex: [[Resistance to change]] is expected to be strongest among middle managers, whose roles are most affected.

everyday.ex: We're getting a lot of [[pushback]] from the Lyon team on the new shift pattern.

informal.ex: Some of the site managers are [[dragging their feet]] on the new process.

collocations: to push back on a proposal
note_fr: « Pushback » (nom) et « to push back on something » (verbe) = objection, résistance : très courant et sans agressivité. « Reticent » = taciturne ; « réticent » se dit « reluctant ».

def: A document setting out who will be told what, when, by whom and through which channel.

formal.ex: The [[communication plan]] provides that employee representatives will be informed before any announcement is made to staff or to the press.

everyday.ex: Can you share the [[comms plan]] before Friday? I want to check the sequencing.

note_fr: Règle française à intégrer au plan et à expliquer au siège : les représentants du personnel d'abord, les salariés ensuite, la presse en dernier. « Comms » est l'abréviation usuelle, toujours au pluriel.

fr: diffuser en cascade (par la ligne managériale)
def: To pass information down through the organisation, level by level, through line managers.

formal.ex: The key messages will be [[cascaded]] to all employees through their line managers within 24 hours of the announcement.

everyday.ex: Managers get the briefing pack at nine and [[pass on]] the message to their teams by lunchtime.

note_fr: « To cascade » est transitif en jargon d'entreprise. Pensez au mouvement inverse : « to feed back up » (faire remonter). « Briefing pack » (UK), « briefing deck » (US).

def: A meeting at which senior management addresses all employees and takes their questions.

formal.ex: An [[all-employee meeting]] will be held on each site on the day of the announcement.

everyday.ex: The CEO is doing a [[town hall]] in Lyon on Thursday, and I'm drafting the talking points.

informal.ex: There's an [[all-hands]] at ten, and nobody knows what it's about.

collocations: to take questions from the floor
note_fr: Rien à voir ici avec la mairie. « All-hands (meeting) », venu de la marine, est très courant dans les groupes américains. « Plenary meeting » est réservé aux congrès et aux institutions.

def: A short list of the main things a speaker should say, and how to say them, on a given subject.

formal.ex: The [[key messages]] have been approved by the Chief Executive and reviewed by legal counsel.

everyday.ex: I'll send you [[talking points]] and a Q&A so that every manager says the same thing.

informal.ex: For now, [[the party line]] is that no decision has been taken.

note_fr: « Language elements » est un calque incompréhensible. « To stay on message » = s'en tenir aux éléments de langage. « The party line » est légèrement ironique.

def: The genuine support of the people whose cooperation is needed to make a project work.

formal.ex: The project cannot succeed without the [[endorsement]] of site management.

everyday.ex: We've got [[buy-in]] from the plant managers, but the unions aren't there yet.

informal.ex: Is the finance director [[on board]]?

note_fr: « Adhesion » = adhérence (de la colle) ! L'adhésion à un projet se dit « buy-in » ou « support ». À ne pas confondre avec le « management buy-in (MBI) », rachat par des dirigeants venus de l'extérieur.

def: The informal circulation of unconfirmed information among employees.

formal.ex: In order to avoid [[speculation]], staff will be informed as soon as the works council meeting has ended.

everyday.ex: The [[rumour mill]] has been in overdrive since the auditors turned up.
everyday.ex_us: The [[rumor mill]] has been in overdrive since the auditors showed up.

informal.ex: I heard on [[the grapevine]] that the site is up for sale.

collocations: to hear something on the grapevine
note_fr: UK « rumour », US « rumor ». « A leak » = une fuite. Une phrase qui porte auprès d'un comité : « If we don't communicate, the rumour mill will fill the vacuum. »

def: The body that governs a company on behalf of its shareholders and to which the chief executive answers.

formal.ex: The [[Board of Directors]] approved the proposed transaction in principle, subject to completion of the employee consultation process.

everyday.ex: I'm presenting the social risks to [[the board]] on Tuesday, and I've got ten minutes.

collocations: to go to the board for approval
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, « director » = administrateur, membre du board : un « HR Director » n'y siège pas forcément. « Board pack » (UK), « board book » ou « board deck » (US) = dossier du conseil.

def: The group of senior executives who run the company day to day under the chief executive.

formal.ex: The proposal was reviewed by the [[Executive Committee]] at its last meeting.
formal.ex_us: The proposal was reviewed by the [[Executive Leadership Team]] at its last meeting.

everyday.ex: I'll take it to [[ExCo]] on Monday.
everyday.ex_us: I'll take it to the [[leadership team]] on Monday.

informal.ex: [[The top team]] is split on the timing.
informal.ex_us: [[The C-suite]] is split on the timing.

collocations: to sit on the executive committee
to take a paper to ExCo
note_fr: « Comex » et « codir » ne sont pas compris : dites « ExCo », « executive committee » ou « leadership team ». « Direction committee » est un calque. « C-suite » = l'ensemble des « Chief ... Officers ».

def: The group of senior people who oversee a project, take the key decisions and resolve the issues escalated by the project team.

formal.ex: The [[steering committee]] meets every two weeks and reports to the Group Chief Executive.

everyday.ex: Let's take that to [[SteerCo]] - it's above my pay grade.

collocations: to take a decision to SteerCo
note_fr: « Pilotage committee » n'existe pas, et « to pilot a project » signifie le tester à petite échelle : piloter se dit « to run », « to lead » ou « to steer ». « Fortnightly » (tous les quinze jours) est britannique ; « biweekly » est ambigu.

def: The senior executive who is ultimately accountable for a project and champions it at the top of the organisation.

formal.ex: The Chief Financial Officer acts as [[executive sponsor]] of the integration project.

everyday.ex: Without a strong [[sponsor]] on the board, the HR workstream will always come last.

note_fr: Double sens à surveiller : en LBO, « the sponsor » est le fonds. « Accountable » (qui répond du résultat) ≠ « responsible » (qui exécute).

def: The people and groups who have an interest in, or can influence, a project or decision.

formal.ex: A map of internal and external [[stakeholders]] is appended to this note.

everyday.uk: everyone with a stake in this
everyday.us: everyone with a stake in this
everyday.ex: Before we announce anything, let's list [[everyone with a stake in this]]: the unions, the mayor, the main customers.

note_fr: « Stakeholder » (partie prenante) ≠ « shareholder » (actionnaire ; US « stockholder »). En France, la liste comprend les élus locaux, la préfecture et l'inspection du travail : à expliciter pour un siège étranger.

def: A significant, dated point in a project that marks the completion of a stage.

formal.ex: The works council's opinion is a critical [[milestone]] on the path to signing.

everyday.ex: We're [[on track]] for the first two milestones, but the third is at risk.

note_fr: « To hit a milestone » = l'atteindre ; « to slip » = glisser. N'employez pas « planning » comme nom : dites « schedule », « timetable » ou « timeline ».

def: A concrete output that a project or assignment is expected to produce by a given date.

formal.ex: The [[deliverables]] for phase one are a risk register, a consultation timetable and a draft communication plan.

everyday.ex: What exactly do you need me [[to deliver]] by the end of the month?

collocations: to deliver on time and on budget
note_fr: « To deliver » s'emploie seul en anglais des affaires (« she delivers » : elle tient ses engagements). « Deliverable » est du jargon projet ; dans un courrier formel, préférez « output » ou nommez le document.

def: One of the parallel strands of work into which a large project is divided, each with its own lead.

formal.ex: The HR [[workstream]] comprises employee relations, payroll, benefits and communications.

everyday.ex: I [[lead on]] employee relations, and Tom has payroll and benefits.

note_fr: En gestion de projet, « chantier » ne se dit ni « yard » ni « construction site ». « To lead on something » (surtout UK) = être responsable d'un sujet ; « owner » = responsable désigné.

def: A table listing the risks to a project, with their likelihood, their impact, the planned response and the person responsible for each.

formal.ex: The [[risk register]] is reviewed at each meeting of the steering committee, and risks rated high are escalated to the Board.

everyday.ex: I've added the strike threat to the [[risk log]] and rated it amber.
everyday.ex_us: I've added the strike threat to the [[risk log]] and rated it yellow.

collocations: to rate a risk high, medium or low
note_fr: « Likelihood » (probabilité) et « impact » (gravité) sont les deux axes. Pour l'orange du feu tricolore : « amber » au Royaume-Uni, « yellow » aux États-Unis. « Risk owner » = porteur du risque.

def: Action taken to reduce the likelihood of a risk or to limit its consequences.

formal.ex: The [[mitigating measures]] proposed include early engagement with the unions and a retention plan for key staff.

everyday.ex: We can't remove the risk of a strike, but we can [[mitigate]] it by starting talks early.

informal.ex: What's our [[plan B]] if the works council asks for an expert?

note_fr: « To mitigate » est transitif : « to mitigate a risk », jamais « mitigate against » (confusion avec « militate against »). « Mitigé » ne se dit pas « mitigated » mais « mixed » : « mixed results ».

def: The decision, taken at a fixed point, whether to proceed with the next stage of a project or to stop.

formal.ex: The [[go / no-go decision]] on the payroll migration will be taken by the steering committee in June.

everyday.ex: We're waiting for [[the go-ahead]] from head office before we convene the works council.

informal.ex: London has finally given us [[the green light]].

collocations: to put a project on hold
note_fr: « The go » seul ne se dit pas : « the go-ahead », « the green light ». « To validate » est plus étroit que « valider » : préférez « to approve » ou « to sign off ».

def: To refer an issue to a higher level of management because it cannot be resolved at the current level.

formal.ex: Any issue likely to delay signing must be [[escalated]] to the steering committee without delay.

everyday.ex: I [[flagged it up]] to the CFO last week, and I still haven't had an answer.
everyday.ex_us: I [[flagged]] it to the CFO last week, and I still haven't heard back.

collocations: to escalate an issue to someone
note_fr: En anglais des affaires, « to escalate » = faire remonter à la hiérarchie, et pas seulement « s'aggraver ». « To make it go up » est un calque de « faire remonter ».

def: The temporary appointment of an experienced executive to run a function or lead a project during a period of change or vacancy.

formal.ex: The Company has engaged an [[interim management]] provider to cover the position of HR Director during the sale process.

everyday.ex: I've been working as an [[interim]] for eight years, mostly on carve-outs and restructurings.

informal.ex: They wanted [[a safe pair of hands]] to get them through the sale.

collocations: to step in at short notice
note_fr: « Transition manager » est un faux ami. Dites « interim manager », « interim HR Director ». À distinguer de « acting HR Director » (salarié interne faisant fonction) et de l'intérim au sens de travail temporaire (« agency work », « temping »).

def: A defined piece of work carried out for a client over a limited period.

formal.ex: The [[engagement]] will run for an initial period of six months and may be renewed by agreement.

everyday.ex: My last [[assignment]] was a nine-month carve-out for a US industrial group.

informal.ex: It's a six-month [[gig]], possibly longer if the sale drags on.

note_fr: « Mission » en anglais = raison d'être (« mission statement ») ou mission militaire, diplomatique, religieuse. Pour une mission de conseil ou de transition : « assignment » ou « engagement ». Lettre de mission = « engagement letter ».

def: The limits of what an interim manager or adviser has been asked to do, and what falls outside it.

formal.ex: Any services falling outside the [[scope of work]] shall be agreed in writing in advance.

everyday.ex: Pay negotiations aren't in my [[remit]], but I'm happy to help if you want to extend it.
everyday.ex_us: Pay negotiations aren't in my [[scope]], but I'm happy to help if you want to extend it.

informal.ex: We need to watch out for [[scope creep]] - this started as a consultation and it's turning into a full reorganisation.
informal.ex_us: We need to watch out for [[scope creep]] - this started as a consultation and it's turning into a full reorganization.

note_fr: « Remit » (nom, accent sur la première syllabe : REE-mit) = champ de responsabilité ; britannique, peu usité aux États-Unis. « Perimeter » se comprend mais sonne continental.

fr: lettre de cadrage, cahier des charges de la mission
def: The document that defines the purpose, scope, authority and reporting lines of an assignment, a committee or a review.

formal.ex: The [[terms of reference]] of the assignment are attached as Appendix 1 and may be varied only with the Chief Executive's written agreement.
formal.ex_us: The [[statement of work]] for the engagement is attached as Exhibit A and may be amended only with the Chief Executive Officer's written consent.

everyday.ex: My [[brief]] was simple: get the consultation done without a strike.
everyday.ex_us: My [[mandate]] was simple: get the consultation done without a strike.

informal.ex: I got my [[marching orders]] from the CEO on the first morning.

collocations: to draw up terms of reference
note_fr: « Cahier des charges » ≠ « book of charges ». « Brief » (nom) = le cadrage donné par le client. Attention : au Royaume-Uni, « to get one's marching orders » signifie aussi se faire renvoyer.

def: The transfer of responsibility, information and open files from one person to his or her successor.

formal.ex: A two-week [[handover]] period is planned with the incoming HR Director.
formal.ex_us: A two-week [[transition]] period is planned with the incoming HR Director.

everyday.ex: I [[hand over to]] my successor on the 30th, and I'd like to walk her through the open files first.
everyday.ex_us: I [[hand off to]] my successor on the 30th, and I'd like to walk her through the open files first.

collocations: to bring someone up to speed
note_fr: Nom en un mot (« handover »), verbe en deux (« to hand over »). « Passing » ou « passation » ne conviennent pas. « To bring someone up to speed » = mettre quelqu'un au courant.

def: Improvements that are easy to achieve and deliver visible results early in a project.

formal.ex: The first ninety days will focus on a small number of [[early, visible improvements]] in order to build confidence.

everyday.ex: Fixing the payslip errors is one of the [[quick wins]] - it costs nothing and everyone notices.

informal.ex: Let's start with the [[low-hanging fruit]] before we tackle working time.

note_fr: « Low-hanging fruit » est indénombrable (jamais « fruits »). Deux expressions de jargon : efficaces à l'oral, à doser à l'écrit.

def: To start a new role or project and be effective straight away.

formal.uk: to be fully effective from the first day
formal.us: to be fully effective from the first day
formal.ex: The assignment calls for a practitioner able [[to be fully effective from the first day]].

everyday.ex: I've done four carve-outs in the last six years, so I can [[hit the ground running]].

informal.ex: I'd rather [[get stuck in]] than spend a month on an audit.
informal.ex_us: I'd rather [[dive right in]] than spend a month on an audit.

collocations: to get up to speed quickly
note_fr: « Operational » appliqué à une personne est un calque : on le dit d'un site ou d'un système. « A steep learning curve » = un apprentissage exigeant et rapide.

fr: gestion prévisionnelle des emplois et des compétences (GEPP, ex-GPEC)
def: The process of working out what jobs and skills a company will need in the coming years and how to close the gap with what it has today.

formal.ex: [[Strategic workforce planning]] will be used to identify the roles at risk and the internal moves available before any restructuring is considered.

everyday.ex: If we do the [[workforce planning]] properly now, we can handle a lot of this through retraining and natural attrition.

note_fr: En France, c'est aussi un thème de négociation périodique obligatoire dans les grandes entreprises : précisez-le, car ailleurs « workforce planning » est une simple pratique de gestion. « Skills » est plus naturel que « competences ».

explain.written: In France, large companies are required to negotiate periodically with their unions on the forward-looking management of jobs and skills (known as GEPP), which makes strategic workforce planning a subject of collective bargaining and not merely a management tool.
explain.spoken: In France workforce planning isn't just an HR exercise: big companies have to negotiate on it with the unions every few years.

def: A company's reputation as a place to work, among its own employees and in the job market.

formal.ex: The Group's [[employer brand]] in France has been weakened by two years of uncertainty over the future of the site.

everyday.ex: Our [[reputation as an employer]] has taken a knock locally, and recruitment is already harder.
everyday.ex_us: Our [[reputation as an employer]] has taken a hit locally, and recruiting is already harder.

note_fr: « Employer brand », jamais « employer mark ». En période de transformation, l'enjeu est moins d'attirer que de retenir : « to retain talent » (indénombrable dans ce sens).

def: The overall picture of the competitors in a market, their relative strengths and their likely moves.

formal.ex: The [[competitive landscape]] has changed significantly since two of the Company's main rivals merged.

everyday.ex: Before we talk about retention, it's worth looking at [[who we're up against]] in the local job market.

collocations: to poach staff from a competitor
note_fr: « Concurrent » en anglais = simultané ; un concurrent est « a competitor », la concurrence « the competition ». « To poach » = débaucher.

def: Small, early indications that a problem is developing, picked up before it becomes obvious.

formal.ex: Absenteeism, resignations and the tone of union leaflets are monitored as [[early warning indicators]] of a deteriorating climate.

everyday.ex: The [[early warning signs]] were all there: sick leave was up, and two of the union reps had stopped talking to us.

informal.ex: They're only [[straws in the wind]], but I'd take them seriously.

collocations: to pick up on a signal
to keep an ear to the ground
note_fr: « Weak signals » existe en prospective mais reste jargonnant ; « early warning signs » est compris de tous. « To keep an ear to the ground » = rester à l'écoute du terrain.

def: The extent to which a company's public image could be damaged by an event or decision.

formal.ex: The closure of the site would carry significant [[reputational exposure]] for the Fund, given the public subsidies received.

everyday.ex: The last thing the fund wants is [[bad press]] in the middle of a fundraising.

informal.ex: It would [[look bad]] if the story broke before the works council had been told.

note_fr: « Image risk » est un calque : dites « reputational risk » ou « reputational exposure ». « Exposure » = degré d'exposition à un risque, qu'il soit financier, juridique ou médiatique.

def: The lawful gathering and analysis of information about competitors, markets and the business environment in order to support decisions.

formal.ex: [[Competitive intelligence]] gathered from public sources suggests that two rival bidders are preparing an offer.

everyday.ex: We [[keep tabs on]] what the competitors are paying, mostly through recruiters and job ads.

note_fr: « Economic intelligence » est un calque qui évoque le renseignement d'État : dites « competitive intelligence » ou « market intelligence ». Veille = « monitoring » ou « watch ».
